Upon detonation of a cased explosive, the casing breaks up into fragments with varying weights and velocities. The destructive potential of these fragments is a function of their shapes, materials, momentum and kinetic energy distributions. Therefore, through testing or analysis, the velocity and weight of the "worst case" fragment must be determined and used for penetration analysis and as a design criterion for fragment barriers.

The most common technique for calculating the initial velocity of fragments in contact with an explosive charge is the Gurney method. The initial velocity of primary fragments resulting from the detonation of a cased explosive is a function of the explosive output and the ratio of the explosive charge weight to casing weight.
